romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-01.question: In Romans 3:23, all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-01.feedbackCorrect: Paul includes everyone in sin and everyone in need of God's glory.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Romans 3:23, which includes everyone in sin.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-01.hint: Look at whom the verse includes.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-02.question: In Romans 3:23, tap what everyone did.
romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-02.feedbackCorrect: All have sinned: Paul's diagnosis leaves no one out.

feedbackWrong.b: God's glory is what everyone falls short of.
feedbackWrong.c: Falling short is the condition; the action stated before is another.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-02.hint: Look for the action assigned to everyone.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-03.question: According to Romans 3:20, through what will no one be justified before God?
romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-03.feedbackCorrect: Works of the law do not justify; the law gives full knowledge of sin.

feedbackWrong.a: Faith in Jesus is the way of righteousness, not what the verse denies.
feedbackWrong.c: Christ's blood appears in 3:25, not as the means denied here.
feedbackWrong.d: Grace justifies freely, according to Romans 3:24.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-03.hint: Read the first part of the verse.

options.b: Through works of the law
options.c: Through the blood of Christ

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-04.question: Put Romans 3:24 together in the order of the text.
romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-04.feedbackCorrect: The order shows a free gift, God's grace and redemption in Christ.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with being justified freely; Christ Jesus closes the verse.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-04.hint: The verse starts with the gift received.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-05.question: In Romans 3:20, what does the law give full knowledge of?
romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-05.feedbackCorrect: The law does not justify; it makes sin known in its fullness.

feedbackWrong.b: Human effort is not the knowledge the law gives here.
feedbackWrong.c: The law produces no merit that justifies before God.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-05.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-06.question: What does Romans 3:23 say that connects to this context?
romanos-sem-rm-01-pecado-06.feedbackCorrect: All have sinned and fall short of glory: no one is enough before God.

feedbackWrong.b: The text says all, leaving no group out.
feedbackWrong.c: The law reveals sin; it justifies no one.

options.b: Only some have sinned
options.c: The law saves on its own

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-01.question: In Romans 3:20-21, God's righteousness was revealed through works of the law.
romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-01.feedbackCorrect: It was revealed apart from the law, though the law bears witness to it.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 3:21, which says apart from the law.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-01.hint: Compare the role of the law in the two verses.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-02.question: In Romans 3:21, tap the word that opens the contrast with what came before.
romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-02.feedbackCorrect: The turn in the argument starts with the word that opens the verse.

feedbackWrong.a: This word marks the new time; it does not open the contrast.
feedbackWrong.b: This is the announced theme, not the turning word.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-02.hint: Look at the start of the verse.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-03.question: How does God's righteousness reach people in Romans 3:21-22?
romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-03.feedbackCorrect: Righteousness is for all and upon all who believe, without distinction.

feedbackWrong.a: The text states there is no distinction among those who believe.
feedbackWrong.b: The context shows everyone sinning and needing this righteousness.
feedbackWrong.c: The text separates it from works of the law in 3:21.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-03.hint: See who receives this righteousness in verse 22.

options.a: It belongs only to a chosen people
options.b: It rewards those who never admitted sin
options.c: It rewards those who keep the law well
options.d: It reaches those who trust in Jesus Christ

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-04.question: How does the argument move in Romans 3:20-22?
romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-04.feedbackCorrect: First the diagnosis, then the announcement, then whom it reaches.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the law revealing sin; those who believe come last.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-04.hint: Its reach to those who believe closes the passage.

options.b: God's righteousness is revealed
options.c: It reaches all who believe

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-05.question: In Romans 3:22, God's righteousness is upon all who do what?
romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-05.feedbackCorrect: Righteousness is upon all who believe, for there is no distinction.

feedbackWrong.b: Working by the law is not the way announced here.
feedbackWrong.c: The verb in the text speaks of believing, not doing works.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-05.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-06.question: What links Romans 3:22 to Habakkuk 2:4?
romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-06.feedbackCorrect: Habakkuk already announced that the righteous will live by faith.

feedbackWrong.b: Romans separates this righteousness from works of the law.
feedbackWrong.c: Both texts place faith at the center of a righteous life.

romanos-cam-rm-01-pecado-06.hint: Compare the means by which righteousness comes.

options.b: Living by works of the law
options.c: Living with no need to believe

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-01.question: Romans 3:24-26 shows God as just in justifying the one who has faith in Jesus.
romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-01.feedbackCorrect: God does not give up justice when he justifies those who have faith in Jesus.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread 3:26, which unites just and justifier in God.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-01.hint: Look at the goal stated in verse 26.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-02.question: In Romans 3:24, tap the word showing that justification costs the sinner nothing.
romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-02.feedbackCorrect: Justification is a free gift, by grace, in Christ Jesus.

feedbackWrong.a: This term names the rescue in Christ, not the cost to the sinner.
feedbackWrong.c: Christ is where redemption is; the free gift comes before.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-02.hint: Look for how the gift is given.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-03.question: What reading does Romans 3:23-24 support about how a sinner is justified?
romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-03.feedbackCorrect: All have sinned, and justification comes freely, by grace, in Christ.

feedbackWrong.b: All have sinned; grace is not limited to those who sinned little.
feedbackWrong.c: The law gives knowledge of sin, not justification, in 3:20.
feedbackWrong.d: The text speaks of a gift by grace, not of one's own merit.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-03.hint: Join the need in 3:23 to the gift in 3:24.

options.a: God justifies by grace those who believe in Christ
options.b: Only those who sinned little can be justified
options.c: The law justifies those who know it well
options.d: Each person is justified by their own merit

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Romans 3:23-26?
romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-04.feedbackCorrect: Everyone's need, the gift of grace and faith in Jesus form the thread.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with everyone's need; faith in Jesus closes the thread.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-04.hint: Follow from the need to the gift and to faith.

options.a: All have sinned and need God
options.b: God justifies by grace in Christ
options.c: Whoever believes in Jesus is justified

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-05.question: In Romans 3:26, God is just and what of the one who has faith in Jesus?
romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-05.feedbackCorrect: God remains just and, at the same time, justifies the one who believes.

feedbackWrong.a: The text states the opposite for the one who has faith in Jesus.
feedbackWrong.c: Accuser is not the role of God stated in this verse.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-05.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-06.question: What links Romans 3:24 to Genesis 15:6?
romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-06.feedbackCorrect: Abraham believed, and it was counted to him as righteousness, as Paul recalls.

feedbackWrong.b: Abraham lived before the law was given at Sinai.
feedbackWrong.c: Genesis ties righteousness to believing, not to earning by works.

romanos-pro-rm-01-pecado-06.hint: See what Abraham did in the Genesis text.

options.a: He believed and God counted it righteousness
options.b: He kept the whole law
options.c: He obeyed and earned righteousness

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-01.question: In Romans 5:1, we have peace with God through our own works.
romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-01.feedbackCorrect: Peace comes through our Lord Jesus Christ, by faith.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 5:1, which points to Jesus Christ as the means of this peace.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-01.hint: See through whom this peace comes.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-02.question: In Romans 5:1, tap what the justified have with God.
romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-02.feedbackCorrect: Justified by faith, we have peace with God in Christ.

feedbackWrong.b: This is the means by which we were justified, not what we have with God.
feedbackWrong.c: Christ is the one through whom we have this relationship with God.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-02.hint: Look for the relationship with God.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-03.question: According to Romans 5:2, to what do we have access by faith through Christ?
romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-03.feedbackCorrect: Through Christ, by faith, we enter this grace and stand firm in it.

feedbackWrong.a: The next verse speaks of tribulations, not their absence.
feedbackWrong.b: Access is by faith, not a prize for our own works.
feedbackWrong.c: The access announced is to God's grace, not to judging others.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-03.hint: Read the start of the verse.

options.a: To a life without any tribulation
options.b: To a prize for our works
options.c: To the right to judge others
options.d: To this grace in which we stand

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-04.question: Put Romans 5:3-4 together in the order of the text.
romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-04.feedbackCorrect: The text's chain goes from tribulation to perseverance and to hope.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with tribulation; hope closes the chain.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-05.question: In Romans 5:4, what does experience produce at the end of the chain?
romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-05.feedbackCorrect: In believers, experience feeds hope in the glory of God.

feedbackWrong.b: The text points forward, not to a worn-out end.
feedbackWrong.c: Paul's chain ends in trust, not in giving up.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-05.hint: Look at the last word of the verse.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-06.question: What does Romans 5:1 say that connects to this context?
romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-06.feedbackCorrect: Whoever is justified by faith has peace with God in Christ.

feedbackWrong.b: The text announces the end of the war for those who believe.
feedbackWrong.c: Peace comes by faith in Christ, not by purchase.

romanos-sem-rm-02-justificacao-06.hint: See the result of being justified.

options.b: War with God forever
options.c: Peace bought by works

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-01.question: In Romans 5:3, tribulation produces giving up in those justified by faith.
romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-01.feedbackCorrect: Tribulation produces perseverance in those who know what God is doing.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 5:3, which names another fruit of tribulation.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-01.hint: See the fruit the verse names.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-02.question: In Romans 5:3, tap the verb linking tribulation to its fruit.
romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-02.feedbackCorrect: This verb shows that suffering, in God, produces something firm.

feedbackWrong.a: This word shows the believer's knowing, not the link between fruits.
feedbackWrong.b: This is the starting point, not the verb that produces fruit.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-02.hint: Look for the action between the two nouns.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-03.question: How does Romans 5:3-4 link together the life of the justified?
romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-03.feedbackCorrect: The chain moves from suffering to firmness, from experience to trust.

feedbackWrong.a: Experience feeds hope, according to the text.
feedbackWrong.c: Future trust appears at the end of the chain, not the start.
feedbackWrong.d: Paul boasts in tribulations precisely because of this fruit.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-03.hint: Follow the order of the fruits in the two verses.

options.b: Suffering with God builds firmness and future trust
options.c: Hoping comes before any inner firmness
options.d: Suffering proves the person's faith has ended

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-04.question: How does the scene move in Romans 5:1-2?
romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-04.feedbackCorrect: Peace with God, access to grace and hope of glory form the progression.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with peace with God; the hoped-for glory closes the passage.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-04.hint: The glory of God is the final horizon.

options.a: Justified, we have peace with God
options.b: By faith, we enter this grace
options.c: Standing firm, we hope for God's glory

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-05.question: In Romans 5:2, how do we stand in this grace we entered by faith?
romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-05.feedbackCorrect: We do not go in and out of grace: in Christ we stand firm in it.

feedbackWrong.a: Access is through Christ, who makes us stand firm in grace.
feedbackWrong.b: Grace sustains the believer; it does not leave them empty.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-05.hint: Look at the state grace keeps us in.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-06.question: What links Romans 5:3 to James 1:3?
romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul and James see trials producing perseverance in believers.

feedbackWrong.a: Faith is tested precisely in the middle of tribulation.
feedbackWrong.b: In both texts, trials produce firmness, not abandonment.

romanos-cam-rm-02-justificacao-06.hint: Compare the fruit in the two texts.

options.b: Trials as a sign of abandonment
options.c: Trials that produce perseverance

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-01.question: Romans 5:3-4 presents tribulation as a path that ends in hope for believers.
romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-01.feedbackCorrect: Paul's chain ends in hope, not defeat.

feedbackWrong.false: Follow the chain to the end, in Romans 5:4.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-01.hint: Follow the chain to the last word.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-02.question: In Romans 5:2, tap the phrase showing the future believers hope for.
romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-02.feedbackCorrect: The believer's future looks toward the glory of God.

feedbackWrong.b: This is the means of access, not the horizon of hope.
feedbackWrong.c: This phrase speaks of present grace, not the hoped-for future.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-02.hint: Look for where hope is looking.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-03.question: What reading does Romans 5:1 support about peace with God?
romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-03.feedbackCorrect: Peace springs from being justified by faith, through Christ.

feedbackWrong.b: Peace is with God and comes through Christ, not from oneself.
feedbackWrong.c: Right after, Paul speaks of tribulations without losing this peace.
feedbackWrong.d: The stated means is faith in Christ, not piled-up works.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-03.hint: Connect the start of the verse to its end.

options.a: It is the fruit of being justified by faith in Christ
options.b: It is a calm a person produces alone
options.c: It depends on never suffering tribulation again
options.d: It is a prize for those who stored up good works

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Romans 5:1-4?
romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-04.feedbackCorrect: Justification, present peace and proven hope form the path.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with being declared righteous; proven hope comes last.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-04.hint: Tribulation appears after the announced peace.

options.a: Declared righteous by faith in Christ
options.b: At peace with God and standing in grace
options.c: Hope that endures through tribulation

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-05.question: In Romans 5:1, what word opens the verse and names who was declared righteous?
romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-05.feedbackCorrect: The verse opens by naming those God declared righteous by faith.

feedbackWrong.a: The text announces the opposite for those who believe in Christ.
feedbackWrong.b: God establishes in grace those he justifies; he does not forget them.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-05.hint: It is the first word of the verse.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-06.question: What links Romans 5:2 to John 14:27?
romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-06.feedbackCorrect: Peace with God comes through Christ, who gives his peace to his own.

feedbackWrong.a: Access is by faith in Christ, not by purchase.
feedbackWrong.b: Romans ties this peace to our Lord Jesus Christ.

romanos-pro-rm-02-justificacao-06.hint: See who gives peace in the John text.

options.b: Peace without any Christ
options.c: Christ gives his peace

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.question: In Romans 8:1, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: For those in Christ Jesus, condemnation is left behind.
romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.hint: Look at the start of the chapter.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.question: In Romans 8:1, tap what there no longer is for those in Christ Jesus.
romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: The sentence of condemnation no longer weighs on those in Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: Christ Jesus is where the person is, not what was removed.
feedbackWrong.b: The Spirit is the one we walk by, not what ceased to be.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.hint: Look for what was taken away.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.question: According to Romans 8:2, what set Paul free from the law of sin and death?
romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: What sets free is the law of the Spirit of life, in Christ Jesus.

feedbackWrong.a: Keeping away from people is not what the verse states.
feedbackWrong.b: Forgetting the past is not the agent named in the verse.
feedbackWrong.d: The text credits freedom to the Spirit in Christ, not to effort.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.hint: Read who acts in the verse.

options.b: Forgetting past sins
options.c: The law of the Spirit of life in Christ

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.question: Put Romans 8:5 together in the order of the text.
romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: The verse contrasts two inclinations and two ways of thinking.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with leaning toward the flesh; the Spirit closes the verse.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.hint: The Spirit appears in the second half.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.question: In Romans 8:2, the law of the Spirit is the law of what, in Christ Jesus?
romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.feedbackCorrect: It is the law of life, which sets free from the law of sin and death.

feedbackWrong.b: Sin belongs to the other law, from which Paul was set free.
feedbackWrong.c: Death belongs to the other law, from which Paul was set free.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.hint: Contrast it with the end of the verse.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-06.question: What does Romans 8:1 say that connects to this context?
romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-06.feedbackCorrect: Being in Christ Jesus changes the sentence: there is no condemnation.

feedbackWrong.a: The verse ties this freedom to walking by the Spirit.
feedbackWrong.c: The text states precisely the end of condemnation in Christ.

romanos-sem-rm-03-vida-espirito-06.hint: See the new situation in Christ.

options.b: No condemnation in Christ
options.c: Condemnation for believers

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.question: In Romans 8:1-2, there is no condemnation because the Spirit of life set free in Christ Jesus.
romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: Freedom from sin and death explains why there is no condemnation.

feedbackWrong.false: Connect 8:1 to the explanation that follows in 8:2.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.hint: Connect the two verses through the explanation.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.question: In Romans 8:2, tap the word that opens the explanation of the previous verse.
romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: Verse 2 begins by explaining why there is no condemnation.

feedbackWrong.a: This is who sets free, not the word that opens the explanation.
feedbackWrong.c: This is one of the powers Paul was set free from.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.hint: Look at the first word of the verse.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.question: How does Romans 8:3-4 present what God did in the face of the law's limit?
romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: What the law could not do, God did by sending his own Son.

feedbackWrong.a: The decisive action in the text is God's, not isolated effort.
feedbackWrong.b: The law's requirement is fulfilled in those who walk by the Spirit.
feedbackWrong.c: The text says the law was weakened by the flesh.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.hint: See who acts in the two verses.

options.a: Each person solves their own sin alone
options.b: God abandoned the law and its requirement
options.c: The law failed because God weakened it
options.d: God sent his Son and condemned sin

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.question: How does the scene move in Romans 8:3-4?
romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: The law's limit, God's action and a new direction of life form the progression.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the law's limit; following the Spirit closes the passage.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.hint: The new direction of life is the end point.

options.a: The law could not set free alone
options.b: God sends his own Son
options.c: Life now follows the Spirit

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.question: In Romans 8:4, we do not live by the flesh, but by whom?
romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.feedbackCorrect: The new life is directed by the Spirit, not by the flesh.

feedbackWrong.b: The flesh is precisely the direction the text denies.
feedbackWrong.c: Sin was condemned by God in Christ, in 8:3.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.hint: Look at the last word of the verse.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-06.question: What links Romans 8:4 to Galatians 5:16?
romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, Paul calls us to walk and live by the Spirit.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts give a clear direction for the new life.
feedbackWrong.b: The flesh is the direction denied in both of Paul's texts.

romanos-cam-rm-03-vida-espirito-06.hint: Compare the direction of life in the two texts.

options.b: Living led by the flesh
options.c: Living led by the Spirit

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.question: Romans 8:1 teaches that those in Christ can live by the flesh with no difference at all.
romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: The same verse ties being in Christ to walking by the Spirit.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of 8:1, about how these people walk.

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-01.hint: Look at how those in Christ walk.

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.question: In Romans 8:1, tap the phrase showing where those without condemnation are.
romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: No condemnation applies to those who are in Christ Jesus.

feedbackWrong.a: This phrase announces the result, not the place in Christ.
feedbackWrong.c: This phrase shows how the person walks, not where they are.

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-02.hint: Look for the person's position in relation to Christ.

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.question: What reading does Romans 8:5 support about a person's inclination?
romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: Each inclination fills the mind with its own things.

feedbackWrong.b: The Spirit gives life and sets free, not isolated effort.
feedbackWrong.c: The text contrasts the two inclinations and their thoughts.
feedbackWrong.d: The contrast is about life direction, not contempt for the body.

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-03.hint: Connect inclination and thought in the verse.

options.a: The mind shows the direction life follows
options.b: Leaning toward the Spirit is pure human effort
options.c: Flesh and Spirit lead to the same thinking
options.d: The material body is evil and must be despised

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Romans 8:1-4?
romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: No condemnation, set free and led by the Spirit is the passage's path.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the sentence removed in Christ; the Spirit closes it.

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-04.hint: Being led by the Spirit is the end point.

options.a: In Christ, no condemnation at all
options.b: Free from sin and death
options.c: A life led by the Holy Spirit

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.question: In Romans 8:3, what did God condemn in the flesh by sending his Son?
romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.feedbackCorrect: God condemned sin; he did not abandon people to the flesh.

feedbackWrong.b: The target named in the verse is quite specific.
feedbackWrong.c: The Son comes in the likeness of flesh; what is condemned is another.

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-05.hint: Look at the target of God's action.

romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-06.question: What links Romans 8:1 to 2 Corinthians 5:17?
romanos-pro-rm-03-vida-espirito-06.feedbackCorrect: Being in Christ is a new creation and the end of the old condemnation.

feedbackWrong.a: In Christ there is real change, not a life with nothing new.
feedbackWrong.c: Paul announces newness for those in Christ.
